lines.t:
Shoot CF cuts in and attacks
<c:ff00ff>before the trigger attack<c>.

Meanwhile, Fighting Crossfire attacks
<c:ff00ff>after the trigger attack<c>.

So in this case, the order is
Shooting CF, trigger attack, Fighting CF.

Also, Crossfire has a trait: if one attack
hits, the next one is guaranteed to {{hit}}.

Using that, even attack {{part|pl}} with low
{{success}} are easier to land.

Also, a target hit by chained Crossfire
can only choose one {{defense}} action.

If you defend the 1st hit with your right
arm, you defend every other hit with it.

In that case, if your right arm is
destroyed, you can't defend or evade.

Crossfire is a hassle to set up, but once
you master it, it can end a Robattle fast.
